question: Does replacing the mean-pair objective with the first-hit head objective improve difficult-family fitting before considering circuit context?
baseline: Complete sealed r4 CandidateMLP; never rerun or overwrite
variable: Ranking loss only: family mean-pair softplus -> family first-hit head softplus

unchanged.data: Existing six TRAIN families only; no added circuits or newly measured labels

new_instrumentation_not_a_second_model_v: INITIAL / per EPOCH / FINAL fitting-only summaries; logs detached from autograd; no outcome access from held family
held_evaluation: Only after persisted freeze and SHA recheck; same old TRAIN LOFO replay, never BLIND/VALIDATION; do not use held score to select epoch, seed or hyperparameters

analysis.fit_denominator_per_family: 5 other held folds x 3 seeds = 15 dependent observations
analysis.primary_held_grid: 5 nonexhaustive families x 3 seeds = 15, seeds not independent families
analysis.s35932: Report separately; 10 actions mean top10 is exhaustive, new head signal is zero. Macro denominator remains unchanged and this difference is disclosed.
analysis.no_hit_cost_rule: Miss costs are recorded but cannot establish speedup; common-hit pairing can be empty and then the paired estimate is null
analysis.decision: First inspect family-specific fitting ranks/hits against frozen r4; report regressions too. A fit improvement does not establish transfer, and unchanged fit is not proof graph data or more circuits would fix it.

required_before_execution: Independent code/evidence review including CUDA warning interpretation
Separate trainer integration and leakage/determinism/receipt tests
New immutable source binding and explicit real-training authorization
Fresh isolated output directory and prelaunch resource check
